BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall position:** The Seller's package does not match our playbook on any of the 16 issues. Two items look like concessions but are not:

- **The 20% cap and 18-month period** match our fallbacks, but Amelia Frost has not given written authority for either. They cannot be accepted.
- **The phrase "applies to all Claims of any nature"** (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) and **"unless expressly stated otherwise"** (cl 12.3/13) would remove our fraud carve-out and fundamental regime without saying so.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority naming this draft, and none has been given. Do not signal it is available.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000. Only the excess over the basket is recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000. Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k with first-dollar recovery.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and an excess-only basket permanently writes off the first AUD 250k of loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a rule that any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Separate periods for fundamental, tax and fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months and delete the default-extension language.**
- **Reason:** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" default would quietly impose 18 months on title, fraud and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** On the Seller's draft, a defect in title to the shares would be recoverable only up to AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price. That is not an administrative point.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out overriding cls 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5.**
- **Reason:** This is a non-negotiable playbook position that no one may waive, and the "any nature" wording is drafted to cover fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5.00pm 22 Sept 2026 (including DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2). DL 1.4 also disclaims any admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure are expressly rejected in our playbook. The specific disclosures in DL 2–10 should stand only if each is fair and specific. DL 1.4 can be accepted only if it does not dilute those specific disclosures.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** The Buyer has no claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete cl 8.3.**
- **Reason:** Constructive "discoverable" knowledge would effectively void the warranties. If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; and
  - never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:**
  - Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%.
  - DL 2 confirms that no final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions has been provided.
  - Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are both expressly insufficient under our playbook.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release of the roughly AUD 3.2m facility, to be provided after Completion (cl 2/7).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds; and
  - effective security releases (DD-003 cl 9.2) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither is in place. The debt-free basis requires payout at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or a deduction, or expressly Seller-funded with an indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion.**
- **Reason:** These are Company obligations triggered by Completion (DL 5). If they are not deducted, the Buyer funds them after Completion. DL 5 also leaves payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs unaddressed, so an indemnity should cover those too.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and described as "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering any failure of title to, or transfer of, the Ironquay Project Materials and related third-party IP claims. The SOW3 cure (payment of every SOW3 fee under DD-004 cl 7.3, plus a confirmatory assignment) must be preserved.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted. Broaden it and keep the cure mechanism.**
- **Reason:** The IP does not transfer until cleared payment, and DL 4 confirms there is no receipt and no assignment. The AUD 180,000 open item in DD-010 is not independently verified, so do not treat the sum as either confirmed or resolved.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Covenants to:
  - preserve logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation (access, scope, and whether notification is required); and
  - provide regular updates before Completion.
  
  The Buyer also wants protection that is not limited by the "not material" characterisation.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation. Add the covenants.**
- **Reason:** DL 6 confirms that access, scope and any notification duty are undetermined for about 1,240 records. We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, and the Seller should not be allowed to pre-empt the answer either.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** The three renewals of AUD 110,000 each are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course, with DD-008 and DD-011 read together, before any treatment is agreed.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet. Request information.**
- **Reason:** DL 8 does not establish any of these points. Our playbook rules out automatic Debt classification or a price deduction, but equally we should not concede ordinary-course treatment unseen.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single general regime covering all Claims ("all Claims of any nature" and "unless expressly stated otherwise"). Tax and IP are treated as settled under it.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants, with no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add an express hierarchy clause** stating that general limitations do not apply to fundamental, tax, specific-indemnity, payment, covenant or fraud claims.
- **Reason:** The Seller's drafting is a hidden override that removes several protections at once.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances (including any Riverlark share security) and authority. Examples:
  - ASIC searches;
  - PPSR searches;
  - original or certified share certificates;
  - Seller board and authority resolutions; and
  - evidence of releases.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DD-012 as sufficient. Request the independent evidence.**
- **Reason:** DD-012 is a Company-maintained internal record. DL 10 itself confirms it is only the source the Seller relies on, not verified proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP kept open as separate regimes, still to be negotiated.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Record both as OPEN.**
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed on either. The mark-up should not concede general-regime treatment, and it should not assert unlimited liability either. Our position is reserved.

---

**Next steps:**
- Return a mark-up restoring our playbook positions on all 16 items.
- Do not use either Amelia Frost fallback (cap or claims period) without her written authority identifying this draft.
- Flag the fraud carve-out and the fundamental regime as threshold issues in the cover note.
